relatedSnapshot.title: Smart views can do everything our Close smart views do, from plain language
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Sales managers should be able to type any view they use in Close today ("my strategy calls today", "my leads whose call outcome was Hot Lead and are still open", "people who attended the webinar and never booked a call") and get the right smart view. This upgrades the model that builds smart views, fixes the gaps that make it refuse or build the wrong view, and adds the call-appointment filters the Close closer views depend on.

## Problem

* The AI cannot use custom dropdown values, cannot build AND/OR groups, and suggestions never use custom fields.
* 13 of our 28 Close smart views (including all 7 numbered closer views) filter on the booked call's type, date, closer and outcome, for example "call outcome is Hot Lead and I am the closer". Our filters only know an appointment's date and owner, not its call type, outcome or attendance.
* The model (Gemini 2.5 Flash) is older and more expensive per token than GPT-6 Luna, and there is no test set that shows whether a change makes smart views better or worse.

## User experience

In the New smart view dialog the user types what they want in plain words. The AI builds the view with the right rules, including custom dropdown values, AND/OR groups, "me" (so each rep sees their own), and conditions on the same booked call (call type, date, closer, outcome, attended or not). The result is an ordinary editable view. If something truly cannot be expressed, the AI says which part and why, as today.

## What's included

* Switch smart view building and suggestions to GPT-6 Luna, with a fallback model, after a 20-prompt comparison against today's model shows Luna is at least as accurate with no new failures. James approved the paid comparison run.
* The 20 prompts come from our real Close smart views plus the examples in this ticket.
* AI can use custom dropdown, multi-select and status values, return AND/OR groups, and use custom fields in suggestions.
* New appointment filters, matched on the same appointment: call type, outcome, attendance, and "no outcome logged". Available in the manual filters and the AI.
* The AI can use the existing appointment date and owner filters (manual-only today).
* Custom date fields get "not in the last N days".
* Teach the AI the phrasing managers use: "today / tomorrow / after tomorrow", "between 3 and 5 days ago", "no activity since", "callable now in their time zone".

Not included (tracked separately): the new filter popover design (ENG-14393), searching every field and notes text ("no mention of refund anywhere"), and new activity fields such as last text or time in stage.

## Done when

* All 20 comparison prompts are recorded with the old and new model's result, and GPT-6 Luna is at least as accurate with no new schema failures.
* Each of the 7 numbered Close closer views can be recreated from one plain-language sentence and returns the same kind of people.
* An AI view using a custom dropdown value, an OR group or "me" opens as an editable view and matches the same records as the equivalent manual view.
* Appointment call type, outcome, attendance and "no outcome logged" work in manual filters on People and Deals.
* Close views we still cannot express are listed with the ticket that will cover them.

## Open questions

* Close treats "has a call outcome of Hot Lead" as any call ever, so a lead can appear in both Ready to Close and Missed Appointments. Recommended default: keep "any matching appointment" (same as Close); add "latest appointment only" later if managers ask.

## Implementation context

AI context.md

relatedSnapshot.title: Smart views can exclude won deals and put no-shows first
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

A manager asked the smart view builder for a "Dormant Leads, 120 Day Revival" list on People: leads from the last 120 days with no contact in 7 days, excluding customers and won deals, with no-shows at the top. The builder declined to build the view and listed three parts it could not express. This closes those gaps so re-engagement lists like this build fully, by hand and from one sentence.

## Problem

The builder returned "Part of this request cannot be filtered yet" with three reasons:

* **Won deals:** the linked deal stage filter on People has no "is none of" option, so "exclude people whose deal is won" cannot be built.
* **No-shows first:** a view cannot be sorted by appointment attendance, so no-shows cannot be put at the top.
* **Appointment outcome:** "No meeting outcome values are configured", so an outcome condition could not be used. This may be workspace setup rather than a missing filter (see Open questions).

## User experience

On People, a manager adds a linked deal stage filter and picks "is none of" with one or more stages (for example every won stage), in the filter popover or by typing "exclude won deals" in the New smart view dialog. They can also sort the list by appointment attendance so people who no-showed come first, then by longest time since last contact. The result is an ordinary editable view, and the builder no longer lists these two parts as unsupported.

## What's included

* "Is none of" on the linked deal stage filter on People, in manual filters, sample data and the smart view builder.
* Sort People by appointment attendance, with no-shows first, usable as the first sort with a second sort after it (for example last contact, oldest first).
* The smart view builder returns the sort with the view. The "Sorted by" display is already listed in ENG-14193.
* Not included: linked deal owner and deal custom fields on People, tracked in ENG-14417.

## Done when

* "People created in the last 120 days, not contacted in 7 days, excluding won deals, no-shows first" builds from one sentence with no "cannot be filtered yet" notice for won deals or no-show ordering.
* The same view can be built by hand in the filter popover and returns the same people.
* A person with a won deal does not appear in a view that excludes won stages.
* Sample data mode gives the same results as the real list.
* The appointment outcome notice is explained: either outcome values were missing in that workspace, or the bug is fixed or ticketed.

## Open questions

* When a person has several deals, does "stage is none of Won" drop them if any linked deal is won, or only if all are? Recommended default: drop them if any linked deal is in an excluded stage, since the goal is to keep customers out of revival lists.
* A person can have several appointments. Which one decides the attendance sort? Recommended default: the most recent past appointment.
* Appointment outcome and attendance filters shipped in ENG-14395, and admins manage the outcome list in settings (ENG-13849). Check whether the workspace that produced the notice has meeting outcomes configured. Recommended default: if it does, treat the notice as a bug in this ticket; if not, no change beyond a clearer message pointing to the setting.

relatedSnapshot.title: Store Floor Command Smart Views against Reporting Views
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Managers can save personal and floor-shared Floor Command Smart Views against the workspace's configured Reporting Views, and each user's last selected Reporting View or Smart View follows them across browsers and devices.

## Problem

Smart Views still store fixed All, Closer, SDR, or Consultancy keys, while the current selection is kept only in browser storage. This can silently use the wrong scope when a Reporting View is renamed, narrowed, disabled, or deleted.

## Proposed fix

Store the canonical `reportingViewId` in Smart Views and persist each user's last Floor Command selection in the database. Resolve the Reporting View first on every open, then intersect the Smart View with the Reporting View and the current viewer's permissions.

## What's included

* Support enabled configured Reporting Views from both trusted templates.
* Let a Smart View use any enabled Reporting View the user can access. Consultant, SDR, and Closer are not required choices.
* Continue reading old Smart Views through the compatibility aliases from Make Floor Command configurable for every workspace.
* Store one user-specific selection per workspace for either a Reporting View or an accessible Smart View.
* Import a valid browser-only selection once when no database preference exists.
* Preserve personal and floor-shared ownership, permissions, versions, and audit behavior.
* Keep Smart View conditions empty in this ticket. Conditions are delivered by the second child ticket.

## Blocked by

Pickup order: 1 of 2.

* Make Floor Command configurable for every workspace, because it provides canonical Reporting View IDs, compatibility aliases, and the permission-safe resolver.

## How it should work

* The Reporting View is the maximum scope. A Smart View can only narrow it.
* New and edited Smart Views store `reportingViewId`. Existing built-in-key Smart Views continue to open and move to the canonical format when edited.
* The base picker lists every enabled Reporting View the user can access.
* If no enabled Reporting View is available, Smart View creation and saving are disabled with a clear setup message and an admin setup path when permitted.
* Renaming a Reporting View does not break a Smart View because the saved ID remains the same.
* Narrowing a Reporting View safely removes unavailable saved scope and explains what changed.
* If the base Reporting View is disabled, deleted, invalid, or inaccessible, the Smart View remains stored but cannot run. It shows a repair state until an authorized editor explicitly chooses a replacement.
* Deleting a Reporting View never deletes dependent Smart Views and never moves them silently to the default or another Reporting View. The deletion confirmation shows affected personal and shared Smart View counts.
* A missing direct Reporting View selection may fall back to the current workspace default with a notice. This fallback never applies to a broken Smart View dependency.
* Selecting a Smart View applies its Reporting View, period, comparison, pipelines, reps, metrics, and filters together.
* Database preference restoration completes before report queries run so a broader default result does not flash first.

## Who can do what

Existing Smart View permissions remain unchanged. Creators manage private views. Creators and workspace owners or admins manage floor-shared views. Other authorized users can select shared views. Only an authorized editor can repair a broken Smart View. No selection or shared view grants additional workspace, Reporting View, pipeline, rep, record, payment, or cash access.

## What the user sees

* The Smart View editor shows configured Reporting Views instead of fixed role choices.
* An empty state explains when Reporting View setup is required.
* A renamed base displays its new name automatically.
* A deleted, disabled, invalid, or inaccessible base shows a clear unavailable message and repair action.
* Direct selections that disappear recover to the default with a notice.
* The last valid selection is restored consistently across devices.

## Done when

- [ ] New and edited Smart Views store a canonical `reportingViewId`.
- [ ] Existing All, Closer, SDR, and Consultancy Smart Views still open through verified compatibility aliases.
- [ ] Any authorized enabled Reporting View can be used as a base, with a safe empty state when none exist.
- [ ] Reporting View rename and narrowing preserve safe Smart View behavior.
- [ ] Disabled, deleted, invalid, or inaccessible Smart View bases fail closed until explicitly repaired.
- [ ] Reporting View deletion preserves dependent Smart Views and shows accurate personal and shared dependency counts.
- [ ] A broken Smart View never falls back to another Reporting View or broadens its data.
- [ ] Direct missing selections may fall back to the enabled workspace default with a notice.
- [ ] Smart View selection applies all saved state atomically.
- [ ] One database preference per user and workspace supports cross-device restoration and safe one-time browser migration.
- [ ] Tenant isolation, current viewer permissions, version conflicts, audit behavior, loading, error, responsive, keyboard, and accessibility states are tested.

## Open questions

None: all required decisions are settled.

## Expected outcome

Managers can rely on Smart Views to stay attached to the intended configured Reporting View, recover safely from configuration changes, and reopen their last selection on any device without ever gaining or silently widening access.

## Implementation context

See AI context.md for the verified current-code gaps, canonical identity decisions, database preference contract, repair behavior, migration direction, and test seams.

relatedSnapshot.title: Add latest-communication smart columns to views
relatedSnapshot.description:
> **Context.** Glossary: master ticket ENG-12174. For THIS ticket: a "smart column" is a computed, read-only column on a list. You are adding three: what the last communication with each person was (one-line summary like "Sent SMS: saw you were interested..."), when it happened, and which teammate had it. Our team uses exactly these columns in Close today to scan a list and see where every conversation stands without opening records. Built on the derived data ENG-12233 creates; the summary line is computed server-side. Why it matters: it turns a list of names into a list of conversations.

**Size:** M · **Design:** pattern-reuse · **Blocked by:** ENG-12233
**How it should look (Close reference):** Smart Fields (latest communication, latest communication date/user, email last opened): <url> (Smart Fields section)
**Audit evidence:** ENG-12178 findings; our team's "Leads for Grabs" Close view uses these columns today.

### Overview

Any contact or deal list can show, per row: what the last communication was (a one-line summary like "Sent SMS: Name 100, i saw you were..."), when it happened, and who on the team had it. Reps scan a list and Company One see where every conversation stands, without opening records.

### Problem

Views have no computed communication columns. The underlying data exists (calls, emails, SMS on the timeline; ENG-12233 adds the derived fields for filtering) but nothing renders a latest-communication summary as a column.

### Solution

Three new built-in columns on contact and deal views, saved with the view like any column: Latest communication (direction icon + type + first line of content), Latest communication date, Latest communication by (team member). Sortable by date. Backed by the ENG-12233 derived data; the summary line is computed server-side with a sensible truncation.

### Scope

* In: the three columns on contact and deal views, sortable by date, saved in views, correct direction/type labels for calls, emails, and SMS.
* Out of scope: email-open tracking columns (needs open-event data wiring; note as follow-up), editing anything from the column, new filters (ENG-12233 owns filters).

### Acceptance criteria

1. A contact view with the three columns shows the correct latest communication (type, direction, snippet), its date, and the teammate involved, matching the record timeline.
2. The same works on deal views (via the deal's linked contact activity).
3. Sorting by Latest communication date orders correctly.
4. The columns save into shared views and appear for every viewer.
5. Rows with no communications show a clear empty state, not blanks that look like errors.

### Design (Name 1)

* 40 · people list view · 41 · companies list view — the list surfaces the latest-communication smart columns land on (column picker via the table header)

Full screen map on master ENG-12174.

relatedSnapshot.description:
> **Audit update (2026-09-01; verified against origin/main** `b56300e23152`**):** The native Name 2 status and blocker relations now reflect the verified current scope. Existing description history is preserved below.

## Goal

Let users create interaction-based Smart Views in plain English.

## What to build

Support requests such as:

* People we have not contacted in 14 days
* Recently contacted People
* Companies with no email in 30 days
* People with a meeting in the next 7 days

AI-created filters must:

* Use the same fields as manual filters
* Stay editable
* Update correctly as time passes
* Keep existing saved views working
* Include the standard verified activation tracking

"Older than 14 days" should exclude records with no interaction. "Not contacted in 14 days" should include them.

## Execution order

Start after both are complete:

* ENG-12586: People and Company interaction fields
* ENG-12588: Column controls and date formats

This can run in parallel with ENG-12590.

## Done when

An AI-created interaction view returns the same records as the equivalent manual view and remains correct as dates change.

relatedSnapshot.title: Filter smart views and AI search by Whop payments and products
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Let any non-client CRM user filter People and Deals by Whop payment and product data, both in smart views and through AI search.

Examples include:

* People or deals with a $27 Whop payment paid yesterday
* Payments that are paid or pending
* Deals that bought the AI Acquisition Incubator or another Whop product

## Problem

Payment details can appear on an individual record, but they are not reliable filters in smart views or AI search. In the Loom, a confirmed $27 purchase is visible on the person, yet the matching Deals view returns zero results.

The current ticket also limits payment amounts to owners and admins. That is no longer required. Every CRM role except client should be able to see and filter by payment amounts within their own workspace.

## Proposed fix

Make Whop payment and product data available anywhere CRM smart-view filters are supported, and give the AI assistant access to the same filters.

Users must be able to combine payment filters with normal CRM filters such as pipeline, owner, or other People and Deal fields.

## What's included

* Whop product
* Payment amount
* Payment date, including relative dates such as today and yesterday
* Payment status, including paid and pending
* People and Deals smart views
* AI search in the smart-view builder, using the same payment filters
* Saved smart views that can be reused by anyone with access to them
* Payment data remains read-only

## How it should work

* A user can use one or several payment filters together.
* Smart views and AI searches return the same matching People or Deals.
* Payment amounts are visible to every CRM role except client. There is no owner/admin-only amount restriction — that was the restriction being removed. Client-role users were never intended to gain payment access here; every existing payment API already refuses them.
* Filters use the current payment and product data linked to the person or deal.
* Empty results are genuine and are not caused by payment fields being unavailable to the view.
* Existing workspace boundaries still apply. A user can never see another workspace's payment data.

## Who can do what

Any CRM user other than a client can view payment amounts and use Whop payment or product filters in smart views and AI search. Owner, admin and ordinary members are all equal here: there is no owner/admin-only amount restriction.

Client-role users are excluded, matching every existing payment API, which already refuses them. They do not see the payment filters at all rather than seeing filters that fail.

This does not allow anyone to create, edit, refund, or otherwise change a payment.

## What the user sees

The smart-view builder offers clear Whop product, amount, date, and status filters. The result count and records update correctly before the view is saved.

AI search in the smart-view builder answers the same questions in plain language and produces the same filters, so the view it creates can be reviewed, edited and saved like any other.

The separate "Ask AI" assistant can read the payments on a person or deal that is already open. It cannot yet search the whole CRM for a payment cohort — see "Accepted for this delivery".

## Done when

* Any non-client CRM user can build and save a People or Deals smart view using Whop product, amount, date, and status filters.
* A view for a $27 payment paid yesterday returns records that have a $27 payment and have a payment paid yesterday. See "Accepted for this delivery" below: those may currently be two different payments on the same record.
* A view for pending payments returns the correct records.
* A view for buyers of the AI Acquisition Incubator, or another selected Whop product, returns the correct records.
* AI search in the smart-view builder can answer the same questions in plain language and produces the same filters a user would build by hand.
* Payment amounts are shown to every CRM role except client.
* Saved payment views can be opened and used by anyone who has access to that view.
* Cross-workspace payment data is never returned.
* No payment write actions are added.

## Accepted for this delivery

Two things were deliberately accepted rather than built, so the filters could ship. Both are known and written down rather than discovered later.

**Payment rules are matched one at a time.** Combining "amount is $27" with "paid yesterday" finds records that have a $27 payment and have a payment paid yesterday. Today those can be two different payments on the same record, so a deal with a $27 payment last month and a $50 payment yesterday will appear. This is how the existing linked-deal filters already behave. Making the rules describe a single payment is a change to how filter groups are compiled, not a small fix.

**Ask AI cannot build payment cohorts.** The smart-view AI search answers all of the questions above. The separate "Ask AI" assistant can read the payments on a person or deal you already have open, but cannot answer "who paid $27 yesterday" across the whole CRM, because its tools take one record at a time. Giving it that needs a new bounded, paginated search tool.

Both are follow-up work. Neither blocks the filters, and both are recorded in the code where they apply.

## Open questions

None. Two decisions were settled during delivery and are recorded above:

* **Client-role users are excluded.** "Regardless of role" meant removing the owner/admin-only restriction on amounts, not granting clients payment access. Clients are refused by every existing payment API, so the filters follow the same rule and are hidden from them.
* **The two items under "Accepted for this delivery"** are follow-up work, not gaps to fix before this ships.

## Expected outcome

Teams can immediately find and work the right buyers using reusable smart views or plain-language AI searches, without manually opening records to inspect their payments.

## Implementation context

* Loom: Building Smart Views and Finding Leads
* CRM Views and AI Search master ticket
* Related AI assistant data-access work

relatedSnapshot.title: Add Floor Command Smart View conditions and consistent results
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Managers can add supported appointment, rebooking, Whop payment, and product conditions to a Floor Command Smart View, preview the matches, and trust that every reporting surface uses the same authorized answer.

## Problem

Floor Command Smart Views currently reject non-empty conditions. There is no condition editor, shared matcher, or guarantee that previews, cards, rows, details, linked records, CSV, and full exports apply the same condition rules.

## Proposed fix

Add a bounded, family-aware condition contract on top of the canonical Reporting View work. Use one resolved context and the same appointment matcher or existing payment-filter planner everywhere the Smart View is previewed or executed.

## What's included

* Add Appointment outcome and Rebooked conditions.
* Reuse the Whop product, payment amount, payment date, and payment status contract from Filter smart views and AI search by Whop payments and products.
* Support AND logic with a maximum of ten conditions.
* Show live match counts for the metric family affected by the current conditions.
* Apply appointment conditions only to appointment-derived metrics and records.
* Apply payment and product conditions only to explicitly supported deal and cash-derived metrics and records.
* Use one authorized resolved context for preview, cards, rows, details, linked records, CSV, and full exports.
* Preserve the 8-hour unknown-attendance grace behavior owned by Floor Command: show booked calls immediately and attendance within 8 hours. The separate Rebooked condition still uses its approved 48-hour rebooking window.
* Nested logic, OR groups, formulas, inferred appointment-to-deal joins, payment mutations, and a second payment-filter language are not included.

## Blocked by

Pickup order: 2 of 2.

* Store Floor Command Smart Views against Reporting Views, because conditions need its canonical Reporting View identity, database-backed selection, atomic Smart View state, and final authorized scope.

## How it should work

* Conditions use AND logic inside the metric family where they apply.
* The Reporting View remains the maximum scope. Conditions run only inside the final Reporting View, Smart View narrowing, and current viewer permissions.
* Appointment and payment conditions are not joined to each other. Mixed dashboards explain which family each condition affects.
* Rebooking uses normalized non-organizer invitee identity and a bounded 48-hour window. A negative Not rebooked result stays pending until that full window has elapsed.
* The 48-hour rebooking window does not change the separate 8-hour grace period for completed calls with unknown attendance.
* Payment rules reuse the existing field keys, validation, derived statuses, date behavior, and linked-deal semantics.
* Relative dates resolve in the Reporting View timezone when the report runs. Explicit dates remain fixed.
* Client-role users do not see payment conditions and cannot execute them through a crafted request.
* Removed, invalid, or inaccessible condition values make only their affected family unavailable until repaired. A condition is never silently dropped in a way that broadens results.
* Preview responses are debounced and race-safe. An older response cannot replace newer edits.
* Current and comparison results use the same normalized condition plan and scope fingerprint.

## Who can do what

Existing Smart View ownership and sharing rules remain unchanged. Authorized non-client CRM users can use supported payment conditions within their existing access. Client-role users cannot discover or execute payment conditions. Selecting or sharing a Smart View never grants Reporting View, rep, pipeline, record, payment, cash, or cross-workspace access.

## What the user sees

* The Smart View editor provides clear field, operator, and value controls for supported conditions.
* Each condition says which metric family it affects.
* A live Matches X of Y preview is shown per affected family where families cannot be combined honestly.
* Loading, empty, invalid, denied, pending-maturity, stale, and error states are clear.
* Broken condition values show a repair message instead of disappearing silently.
* Cards, rows, details, linked records, CSV, and exports agree for the same Smart View.

## Done when

- [ ] Smart Views store zero to ten valid AND conditions and continue reading earlier Smart View versions.
- [ ] The approved no-show and not-rebooked example can be previewed, saved, reopened, shared, and applied.
- [ ] Rebooking identity, anchor, candidate rules, maturity, and exact 48-hour boundary are shared across preview and production execution.
- [ ] ENG-13388's immediate booking visibility and 8-hour unknown-attendance grace remain unchanged.
- [ ] Whop product, amount, date, and status rules reuse ENG-12239's contract.
- [ ] Client-role users cannot discover or execute payment conditions.
- [ ] Appointment conditions affect only supported appointment results, and payment conditions affect only supported deal or cash results.
- [ ] Invalid or inaccessible conditions fail closed for their affected family and never silently broaden results.
- [ ] Preview uses the same canonical scope, permissions, matcher, planner, timezone, and readiness rules as saved execution.
- [ ] Current and comparison cards, rows, details, linked records, CSV, and full exports reconcile for every supported family.
- [ ] Exact boundaries, tenant isolation, permissions, race handling, responsive states, keyboard behavior, and accessibility are tested.

## Open questions

* Confirm the first Appointment outcome values. Recommended default: Took place, Prospect no-show, Host no-show, Cancelled, and Unmarked.
* Confirm the rebooking anchor. Recommended default: effective cancellation time for cancellations, otherwise the original appointment start time.
* Confirm mixed-family preview. Recommended default: show a separate Matches X of Y count for each affected family because there is no approved appointment-to-deal join.
* Confirm whether Payment Support metrics accept payment conditions. Recommended default: leave Payment Support and other unmapped families unaffected until their source mapping is explicitly supported.

## Expected outcome

Managers can build focused Floor Command Smart Views with trustworthy condition previews and receive the same permission-safe result everywhere the report is viewed or exported.

## Implementation context

See AI context.md for the verified condition gaps, family boundaries, payment-contract reuse, attendance and rebooking distinction, execution direction, open product decisions, and test seams.

relatedSnapshot.title: Make Floor Command smart views use configured reporting views
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Managers can save a personal or shared Floor Command view inside a workspace's configured reporting view, add supported appointment or payment conditions, and trust that previews, dashboard results, record lists, details, and exports all use the same authorized scope.

## Problem

Saved views currently point at fixed All, Closer, SDR, or Consultancy keys. They cannot safely survive a workspace replacing those built-ins with its own reporting views. The condition work also needs one clear rule for mixed dashboards: appointment conditions must not pretend to filter cash, and payment conditions must not pretend to filter call activity.

## User experience

A manager selects one of the workspace's configured reporting views, chooses a period, comparison, reps, metrics, and supported conditions, then sees a live match count before saving. Personal and floor-shared views reopen inside that canonical view. If an admin later renames, disables, narrows, or deletes part of the configuration, the saved view explains what changed and offers a repair path instead of widening access or silently substituting another view.

## What's included

* Store a canonical `reportViewId` in personal and shared Floor Command saved views.
* Continue reading existing saved views that use fixed built-in keys and migrate them through the compatibility aliases from ENG-13207.
* Keep the approved Appointment outcome and Rebooked conditions, live Matches X of Y preview, and shared appointment matcher from the original ticket.
* Reuse the CRM payment and product filter contract delivered by ENG-12239 instead of building another payment-filter language.
* Apply appointment conditions only to appointment-derived metrics and records.
* Apply supported payment and product conditions only to deal and cash-derived metrics and records.
* Show the metric family affected by each condition when a dashboard mixes calls, deals, and cash.
* Intersect saved reps, pipelines, metrics, filters, and conditions with the canonical reporting view and the viewer's current permissions every time it opens.
* Use the same resolved saved-view context for preview, cards, rows, details, linked record lists, CSV, and full exports.
* Arbitrary nested logic, custom formulas, inferred appointment-to-deal joins, and a second payment-filter implementation are not included.

## Blocked by

* Make Floor Command configurable for every workspace, because saved views need the canonical report-view identity, compatibility aliases, and resolver.
* Filter smart views and AI search by Whop payments and products, because Floor Command must consume its validated payment filter contract rather than duplicate it.
* Share Floor Command views, because shared-view persistence and permissions must be settled before this ticket migrates both personal and shared saved views.
* Save personal Floor Command views is the completed saved-view foundation.

## How it should work

* Conditions use AND logic inside their supported metric family.
* The reporting view establishes the maximum workspace scope. A saved view can only narrow it.
* A rolling period remains rolling in the reporting timezone; an explicit range remains fixed.
* Selecting a saved view applies its report view, period, comparison, reps, metrics, filters, and conditions atomically.
* Removed or inaccessible configuration is omitted with a clear warning and edit path. It never silently widens the report or falls back to an unrelated reporting view.
* Preview and report requests use the same matcher, filter contract, and resolved context. Stale preview responses cannot replace newer edits.
* Mixed dashboards state clearly which conditions affect appointment metrics and which affect deal or cash metrics.

## Who can do what

Existing saved-view permissions remain unchanged. Creators manage private views; creators and workspace owners/admins manage floor-shared views; other authorized users can select shared views. Sharing or selecting a view never grants new Floor Command, rep, pipeline, record, payment, or cash access.

## Done when

- [ ] A manager can save, reopen, edit, and share a view that references a configured workspace reporting view.
- [ ] Existing built-in-key saved views continue to open through a verified compatibility path.
- [ ] The approved no-show and not-rebooked example can be created, previewed, saved, reopened, and applied.
- [ ] Supported Whop product, amount, date, and status filters reuse ENG-12239's contract and return the same authorized deals or cash records.
- [ ] Appointment conditions never masquerade as cash or deal filters, and payment conditions never masquerade as call filters.
- [ ] Preview, cards, rows, details, linked records, CSV, and full exports reconcile for each supported metric family.
- [ ] Admin changes to the canonical view produce a repairable warning and never widen or silently substitute data.
- [ ] Permission intersection, deleted configuration, stale previews, exact 48-hour boundaries, dark mode, narrow layouts, keyboard behavior, and accessible touch targets are covered.

## Implementation context

See AI context.md for the implementation evidence, settled dependencies, compatibility decisions, and test seams.

## Name 3 sales-area integration

Existing Reporting View identity, sharing, saved conditions and personal preferences remain the implementation. The configurable sales-area consumer change adds V4 selection compatibility and area/pipeline navigation to that store. It does not recreate Reporting Views or the condition engine.

Delivered through the shared foundation (ENG-12451) and the approved consumer plan (ENG-12261).

relatedSnapshot.title: Add payment-link activity and complete payment filters to Smart Views
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Let CRM users build People and Deals Smart Views using the payment and payment-link data already available in Acquisity, including link engagement, payment terms, refunds, failures and buyer details. Add total-spend and payment-count filters, and let users require several conditions to match the same payment.

## User experience

From People or Deals, open the Smart View filter builder, choose payment or payment-link conditions, preview the matching records, then save and reopen the view. The Smart View's plain-language search must produce the same editable filters and results as manual filtering. Conditions can be combined with existing CRM fields and saved/shared using current view permissions.

## What's included

* Link engagement: opened/not opened, first and last opened date, total opens and unique visitor count.
* Link lifecycle: status, creation date and last copied date. Distinguish no link from an existing link that has never been opened or copied.
* Payment plan: one-off, subscription or split pay; contract and annualized value, initial and renewal amounts, billing interval, required instalment count, trial and configured expiry period where captured.
* Payment method used, separately from the methods offered on the link.
* Refund amount and date; failure date and reason; dispute date. Existing refunded, partially refunded, failed and disputed status filters remain available.
* Fees, net received and payment currency.
* Link creator and recorded owner/closer at payment time, including the existing attribution override where applicable. Do not substitute the deal's current owner for historical payment ownership.
* Checkout buyer name, email and phone, separately from linked CRM contact fields; support finding a captured buyer email that differs from the linked contact.
* Total paid and payment count across the record's linked payments, with an explicit time window and currency.
* Same-payment matching: an amount, date, status and product condition intended to describe one payment must all match that payment. Likewise, combined link conditions must refer to the same link; link-plus-payment conditions must use that link's associated payments.

This extends the completed payment-filter foundation. The separate Floor Command conditions ticket owns dashboard condition rollout. Do not expand this ticket into dashboard redesign, new provider integrations, payment mutations or a separate Ask AI CRM-wide search tool.

## Execution order

Use the lowest-numbered eligible ticket first. Tickets explicitly grouped as parallel may start together when there is capacity, but they still keep the priority order below. Waves show the earliest dependency unlock, not a barrier: start a later-wave ticket as soon as its own blockers are complete.

### Wave 1: can start now

Parallel: none. All three extend the same payment planner, compiler, field registry and parity test suites, so run them one after another in priority order.

1. Filter Smart Views by payment-link opens, status and creator: link engagement and lifecycle fields.
2. Filter Smart Views by payment method, refunds, failures, plan terms and buyer details: remaining per-payment fields and the plan-terms join.
3. Filter Smart Views by total paid and payment count over a time window: totals across payments with currency and window.

### Wave 2: starts when tickets 1 and 2 are complete

Parallel: none.

4. Match combined payment and link conditions against the same record in Smart Views: blocked by ENG-13483 and ENG-13484.

Cross-wave overlap: none verified. Ticket 4 changes how filter groups compile and ticket 3 adds a family to the same builder, so 4 should not overlap 3.

## How it should work

* Make the difference between “one matching payment/link” and “totals across payments” clear in the editor and generated filters.
* A deal with a $27 payment last month and a $50 payment yesterday must not match “a $27 payment paid yesterday” when same-payment matching is selected.
* Handle missing provider data explicitly. Unknown method, fee, buyer details or tracking history must not be invented or silently treated as zero, not viewed, or a mismatch.
* An open event proves a link was opened, not that the named contact personally opened it. Preserve that distinction in labels and results.
* Never add different currencies together without an explicit conversion policy. Avoid double-counting a payment through multiple contact/deal relationships.
* Define gross paid, net received, refunds and qualifying payment statuses clearly. Relative dates use the view's existing timezone rules.
* Existing saved views must not silently change their matching meaning. Provide an explicit, understandable route to the new same-payment behavior.
* Preview counts, list results, saved execution and Smart View plain-language search agree. Invalid or inaccessible filters show a repair/error state rather than disappearing and broadening the results.

## Who can do what

Preserve existing payment-filter access: authorized non-client CRM users can filter within their current workspace and record access; client-role users cannot discover or execute payment filters. Shared views never grant additional access. Payment data remains read-only, and no raw provider payloads, credentials or full card details are exposed.

## Done when

* Every field group listed above can be selected, combined, previewed, saved and reopened in People and Deals Smart Views.
* “Link opened but not paid”, “never-opened existing links”, “payments failed today”, “refunded more than $500 this week” and “subscriptions paid by bank” return the correct records when data is present.
* Total-spend and payment-count filters work together over the chosen time window and currency, with documented refund/status treatment.
* Same-payment and same-link tests reject matches assembled from unrelated payments or links.
* Plain-language Smart View search produces inspectable filters with the same results as manual creation.
* Existing views, grouping/exclusion, timezone boundaries, missing data, duplicate links, attribution changes, sharing and client/cross-workspace access are covered by tests.
* Browser QA proves create, edit, save, reopen and share flows, including empty, loading and error states. Use the repository's activation-tracking skill for the changed user-facing flow and verify events land before counting tracking as complete.

## Implementation context

AI context.md contains the inspected code, field mapping, matching limitations and suggested test coverage.

relatedSnapshot.title: Filter Smart Views by payment-link opens, status and creator
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Reps can build People and Deals Smart Views from what happened to a payment link: whether it was opened, when, how often, its status, when it was created or last copied, and who created it.

## Problem

Payment links already record opens, visitors, status and copy history, but none of it can be used to filter a list. A closer who wants "everyone who opened their link but has not paid" has to open each link.

## Proposed fix

Add link engagement and lifecycle conditions to the Smart View filter builder for People and Deals. They combine with existing fields, preview, save, reopen and share like any other condition, and plain-language search produces the same editable conditions.

## What's included

Opened / not opened, first opened date, last opened date, total opens, unique visitor count, link status, link created date, last copied date, link creator.

Excludes payment detail fields, totals, and same-record matching, which are separate children of ENG-13462. No changes to how links are tracked.

## Blocked by

None: can start immediately.

## How it should work

* A record with no payment link is different from a record whose link exists but was never opened or copied. "Not opened" matches existing links with no opens and never matches records with no link.
* An open proves the link was opened, not that the named contact opened it. Labels say "link opened", never "contact opened".
* Each condition is answered by any one of the record's links. People reach links through their linked deals; Deals use their own links.
* Relative dates follow the view's existing timezone rules.
* An unfinished condition is ignored. A condition the system cannot evaluate returns no rows and shows the existing invalid-filter state.

## Who can do what

Same as the existing payment filters from ENG-12239: non-client CRM users with payment access can pick and run these conditions within their workspace. Client-role users cannot see or execute them, and a shared view grants no extra access.

## What the user sees

The new fields appear in the filter picker under a payment-link group, with plain labels and operators appropriate to each type. Preview counts update as conditions change. Reopening a saved view shows the same conditions. An invalid or inaccessible condition shows the repair state instead of silently widening the list.

## Done when

- [ ] Every listed field can be selected, combined, previewed, saved, reopened and shared in People and Deals views.
- [ ] "Link opened but not paid" and "existing links never opened" return the correct records.
- [ ] Records with no link never match "not opened" or "not copied".
- [ ] Plain-language search produces the same editable conditions and the same results.
- [ ] Preview count, list, saved execution and sample mode agree for every field and operator.
- [ ] Client-role and cross-workspace requests fail closed.
- [ ] Browser QA covers create, edit, save, reopen and share, and activation events are verified.

## Open questions

None: all required decisions are settled.

## Expected outcome

Link engagement follow-up is a saved view instead of a manual check.

## Implementation context

* This ticket's context: AI context.md.
* Parent context: AI context.md on ENG-13462.
* Link tracking fields are written by the public link view route and the copy-link mutation; they exist on the payment link record, not on payments.

relatedSnapshot.title: Master: Smart views match what the sales team had in Close and stay fast
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

The sales team is moving off Close. On 2 October we recreated their Close smart views in the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace: 16 of 28 now exist as shared People views, and 12 could not be rebuilt. This master collects the work that closes those gaps and makes the slow filters fast, so reps can build and trust the same working lists they had in Close.

## Problem

* Most calendar bookings are not attached to a person, so "my calls today" style views miss about two thirds of calls.
* Ten of the 16 views rely on a filter that can only be created through the API. In the filter editor it shows as "This field is no longer available".
* Meeting filters take 4 to 34 seconds on a workspace with 157,000 people, and can fail with "Failed to fetch people".
* The database expects about 4,800 people for a status filter that matches 137,000, so combined views pick slow plans.
* Views that depend on when someone was last contacted cannot be trusted for people imported from Close.

## What's included

* Seven tickets, each delivered as one PR, plus one data task with no PR.
* Speed was measured on the People list only. Deals views and the Deals board use the same filters through a different query shape and should be measured with the same method before the speed tickets are closed.
* Already owned elsewhere, so not repeated here: filtering People by their deal's owner, deal fields and import is Filter People by their deal's owner and deal fields, and by how they were imported. General list speed is under Master: Acquisity loads fast however big a workspace gets.
* Not included: searching emails and texts for a word (parked; it affects one view by 20 people and is the largest piece of work).

## Execution order

Use the lowest-numbered eligible ticket first. Tickets grouped as parallel may start together when there is capacity, but they keep the priority order below. Waves show the earliest dependency unlock, not a barrier: start a later-wave ticket as soon as its own blockers are complete.

### Wave 1: can start now

Parallel: priorities 1, 2, 6 and 8 can all run together. Priorities 4 and 5 both change the filter editor and compiler, so run those two one after the other.

* **Priority 1:** CRM list filters get accurate database statistics and the indexes they are missing. Database only, no application code. One PR.
* **Priority 2:** Calendar bookings are attached to the person and deal they belong to. Link at the source, plus the backfill script. One PR.
* **Priority 4:** Build and edit activity filters in the filter editor, on People and Deals. Reps can build and edit the views that were created through the API. One PR.
* **Priority 5:** Saved view filters return the right people in five edge cases. Small correctness fixes. One PR.
* **Priority 6:** Saved view counts are capped and sorting by latest communication is fast. The total stops costing as much as the page. One PR.
* **Priority 8:** Imported Close history counts towards last contacted, and the fixed Close lists come over. Data task, no PR.

### Wave 2: starts when the booking link is done

Parallel: none in this wave.

* **Priority 3:** Meeting filters load in under a second on large workspaces. Blocked by Calendar bookings are attached to the person and deal they belong to. One PR.

### Wave 3: starts when the meeting filters are done

Parallel: none in this wave.

* **Priority 7:** Filter by call, email and text counts and next meeting without a wait. Blocked by Meeting filters load in under a second on large workspaces. One PR.

Cross-wave overlap:

* Priority 3 may start as soon as priority 2 is done and may overlap priorities 1, 6 and 8 if they are still underway. It changes the filter compiler, so do not run it at the same time as priority 4 or 5.
* Priority 7 may overlap priorities 1 and 8. It also changes how list filters and sorting read stored dates, so do not run it at the same time as priority 6.

## Done when

* A closer opening "Closing Calls - Today" sees every call booked with them today, without relying on imported Close records.
* A manager can build and edit every one of the 16 recreated views in the filter editor.
* Every recreated view, and each single filter measured on 2 October, loads in under 3 seconds on the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace.
* "1 June onwards Farm" and "Money List" can be recreated and return the people Close returned.

## Open questions

* How should closers record a call outcome in Acquisity once Close is off? Five views read Close's imported "Strategy call outcome" history and will stop updating. Recommended default: set up meeting outcomes on appointments to match Close's list and make logging the outcome part of ending a call. Decision for James and Name 4; repointing the five views then becomes part of the activity filter ticket.

relatedSnapshot.title: Match combined payment and link conditions against the same record in Smart Views
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When a rep describes one payment or one link with several conditions, the view only matches records where a single payment or link satisfies all of them.

## Problem

Today each payment condition is answered independently. A deal with a $27 payment last month and a $50 payment yesterday matches "amount is 27 AND paid yesterday". The list looks right and is wrong.

## Proposed fix

Add an explicit same-record mode to filter groups containing payment or link conditions. In that mode, payment conditions in the group must hold for one payment, link conditions for one link, and link-plus-payment conditions for that link's own payments. Existing saved views keep their current behavior until a rep opts in.

## What's included

The same-record mode, its editor control, its saved representation, plain-language search support, and the compatibility rule for existing views. Applies to the fields from ENG-13483 and ENG-13484 plus the four existing payment fields from ENG-12239. Totals from ENG-13485 are unaffected because they are not per-record conditions.

## Blocked by

* ENG-13483: link opens, status and creator filters.
* ENG-13484: method, refunds, failures, plan terms and buyer detail filters.

## How it should work

* Same-record mode is a property of a filter group.
* Positive conditions are correlated. Negated conditions stay independent because correlating them changes the question.
* Two conditions on the same field in one group describe two payments and are not forced onto one row.
* Existing saved views load with the mode off and produce the same results as before. New payment groups default the mode on.
* Plain-language search turns the mode on when the phrasing describes one payment or one link.
* A group that cannot be compiled in same-record mode returns no rows and shows the repair state.

## Who can do what

Same as the existing payment filters. Toggling the mode is an edit to the view and follows view edit permissions.

## What the user sees

A visible control on the group, worded like "Match the same payment", with a short explanation of what changes. Chips read the same in both modes. Preview counts change immediately when the mode is toggled.

## Done when

- [ ] A deal with a $27 payment last month and a $50 payment yesterday does not match "amount is 27 AND paid yesterday" in same-record mode, and does match with the mode off.
- [ ] Combined link conditions must refer to one link; link-plus-payment conditions use that link's own payments.
- [ ] Existing saved views load unchanged and return the same results as before.
- [ ] Plain-language search sets the mode and produces inspectable conditions with matching results.
- [ ] Preview, list, saved execution and sample mode agree in both modes.
- [ ] Exclusion groups, timezone boundaries and duplicate links are covered by tests.
- [ ] Browser QA and verified activation events cover toggle, save, reopen and share.

## Open questions

* Whether new payment groups default the mode on. Recommended default: on for new groups, off for existing saved views until edited.

## Expected outcome

Combined payment and link conditions describe one record, and old views keep meaning what they meant.

## Implementation context

* This ticket's context: AI context.md.
* Parent context: AI context.md on ENG-13462.
* The appointment filters already correlate several positive rules onto one appointment, keyed by attribute. That is the precedent, but it is flat; link-plus-payment needs a nested correlation from a link to its payments.
* The mode must be serialized with the saved view and round-trip through the editor, the plain-language reconciliation, and sample mode.

relatedSnapshot.title: Filter Smart Views by total paid and payment count over a time window
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Reps can filter People and Deals by how much a record has paid and how many payments it has made, within a chosen time window and currency.

## Problem

Today the amount filter looks at one payment at a time. There is no way to find "customers who spent over $5,000 this year" or "buyers with three or more payments".

## Proposed fix

Add totals conditions to the Smart View filter builder: total paid, net after refunds, and payment count, each scoped to a time window and one currency.

## What's included

Total paid, net after refunds and payment count over the record's linked payments; a required currency; an optional time window using the existing relative and absolute date operators.

Excludes per-payment fields and same-record matching, which are separate children of ENG-13462. No currency conversion.

## Blocked by

None: can start immediately.

## How it should work

* Total paid sums the gross paid amount of every payment that was actually paid, meaning status Paid, Partially refunded, Refunded or Disputed. Net after refunds subtracts the refunded amount. Payment count counts the same set. Pending, failed, canceled and voided payments are excluded.
* Only payments in the chosen currency are included. Other currencies are ignored, never converted.
* A payment reached through several contacts on one deal is counted once.
* The time window applies to the paid date and follows the view's existing timezone rules.
* A record with no qualifying payments has a total of zero and a count of zero, so "total paid less than 100" matches it.
* The editor makes clear these are totals across payments, not a single payment.

## Who can do what

Same as the existing payment filters from ENG-12239.

## What the user sees

A totals group in the filter picker with amount, currency and window inputs. The chip reads like "Total paid in USD over the last 90 days is greater than 5,000". Preview and saved views behave as today.

## Done when

- [ ] Total paid, net after refunds and payment count can be selected, combined, previewed, saved, reopened and shared.
- [ ] Totals and count work together over the chosen window and currency.
- [ ] Refund and status treatment is documented in the field description and matches the results.
- [ ] Mixed-currency records only count payments in the chosen currency.
- [ ] A payment linked through two contacts counts once.
- [ ] Preview, list, saved execution and sample mode agree.
- [ ] Client-role and cross-workspace requests fail closed.
- [ ] Browser QA and verified activation events cover the changed flow.

## Open questions

* Which statuses qualify and how refunds are treated. Recommended default is the rule in "How it should work": gross paid over Paid, Partially refunded, Refunded and Disputed; net subtracts refunds; the count uses the same set.

## Expected outcome

Lifetime and period spend segmentation works from the view builder.

## Implementation context

* This ticket's context: AI context.md.
* Parent context: AI context.md on ENG-13462.
* The existing communication count filters are the nearest precedent for an aggregate family. At the People grain the sum must run over a distinct payment set, not over the contact-to-deal junction.

relatedSnapshot.title: Filter Smart Views by payment method, refunds, failures, plan terms and buyer details
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Reps can filter People and Deals by the details of a payment: how it was paid, refunds, failures, disputes, fees and net, currency, the plan it was sold on, who owned it at payment time, and who the buyer said they were at checkout.

## Problem

The CRM stores these details on every payment but only amount, date, status and product can be filtered. "Payments that failed today", "refunded more than $500 this week" and "subscriptions paid by bank" are not possible without opening each payment.

## Proposed fix

Add the remaining per-payment fields to the Smart View filter builder for People and Deals, including plan terms read from the link version the payment was made against.

## What's included

* Payment method used, refund amount, refund date, failure date, failure reason, dispute date, fee amount, net received, payment currency.
* Link creator at payment and deal owner at payment, with the existing closer override applied.
* Buyer name, buyer email, buyer phone.
* Plan terms: schedule type (one-off, subscription, split pay), contract value, annualized value, initial amount, renewal amount, billing interval, required instalment count, trial period and expiry period.
* Existing refunded, partially refunded, failed and disputed status filters stay as they are.

Excludes link engagement fields, totals and same-record matching, which are separate children of ENG-13462.

## Blocked by

None: can start immediately.

## How it should work

* Each condition is answered by any one payment on the record.
* Missing provider data is unknown. A payment with no recorded method, fee, buyer detail or plan does not match a positive condition and does not match a negated one either; it matches only "is unknown" style operators where offered.
* Plan terms come from the link version the payment was made against. Manually recorded payments have none and read as unknown.
* Ownership fields use the values recorded at payment time, never the deal's current owner.
* Buyer email is compared against the contact's canonical email so reps can find a buyer whose checkout email differs from the linked contact.
* Method used is separate from the methods offered on the link.
* Relative dates follow the view's existing timezone rules.

## Who can do what

Same as the existing payment filters from ENG-12239. No raw provider payloads, credentials or full card details are exposed; card brand and last four are not offered as filters.

## What the user sees

The new fields appear in the filter picker under a payments group. Amounts are entered in whole currency units. Select fields list only the values the workspace has. Previews and saved views behave as today.

## Done when

- [ ] Every listed field can be selected, combined, previewed, saved, reopened and shared in People and Deals views.
- [ ] "Payments failed today", "refunded more than $500 this week" and "subscriptions paid by bank" return the correct records.
- [ ] A payment with no recorded method, fee or buyer detail matches neither the positive nor the negated condition.
- [ ] Manual payments read plan terms as unknown.
- [ ] Attribution filters use payment-time ownership and the closer override, not the deal's current owner.
- [ ] Preview count, list, saved execution and sample mode agree for every field and operator.
- [ ] Client-role and cross-workspace requests fail closed.
- [ ] Browser QA and verified activation events cover the changed flow.

## Open questions

* Which contact email buyer-email comparison uses when a contact has several. Recommended default: the canonical contact email only.

## Expected outcome

Payment follow-up on failures, refunds, disputes and plan types is a saved view.

## Implementation context

* This ticket's context: AI context.md.
* Parent context: AI context.md on ENG-13462.
* Schedule type and plan terms are not stored on the payment. They live on the payment link version the payment references, so this ticket adds that join. Manual payments have no version.
* Method, buyer phone, dispute date and link creator at payment are each written from a single place in the provider webhook path, so production coverage should be confirmed before promising negated filters on them.
